q-14364.problem:
If the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(-5,3)$ and $(a,b)$ is $(1,4),$
then $a+b=$
q-14364.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(-5,3)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})},$ ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(1,4)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}\,.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (1,4) & =(\frac{-5+a}{2},\frac{3+b}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}1=\frac{-5+a}{2} \\ 4=\frac{3+b}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}a=7 \\ b=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $(a,b)=(7,5)$ and $a+b=12.$
